observation_value_or_blocker: In female C57BL/6 mice with T10 weight-compression SCI (20 g for 1 minute), a single intrathecal RvD3 injection (1 microgram/20 microliters at 1 hour) improved BMS locomotor recovery, reduced thermal hyperalgesia and lesion area, lowered inflammatory cytokine/chemokine expression, shifted macrophage markers toward an M2-associated pattern, preserved tight-junction proteins, and reduced glial/fibrotic scar markers. In LPS-treated RAW264.7 cells and hCMEC/D3 endothelial cells, RvD3 reduced inflammatory/NO outputs and increased migration or angiogenic-associated markers.

Do not infer a cognate receptor, receptor-proximal relay, or terminal TF: the authors explicitly state that the detailed G-protein receptor mechanism was not investigated and that unique RvD3/RvD4 receptors remain unresolved.

context_and_limitations: The paper tests RvD3 pharmacology and functional outputs but no receptor blockade, genetic perturbation, purified binding, or intracellular relay. The authors discuss GPR32 from prior literature but explicitly state that the detailed RvD3 mechanism was not studied; RAW264.7 and hCMEC/D3 comparator results are not equivalent to the mouse SCI lesion context.

observation_value_or_blocker: In adult mice with contusive SCI, PAR1-null animals showed reduced neutrophil infiltration and blood-spinal-cord barrier disruption at the lesion, improved locomotor and inclined-grid performance, greater white-matter sparing, and reduced glial scarring. Acute recombinant APC improved locomotor recovery in wild-type mice but did not add benefit in PAR1-null mice, supporting PAR1 dependence of the APC functional effect and the paper's biased-agonism interpretation. The study did not measure purified APC-PAR1 binding or define a complete intracellular relay in the injured cord.

claim_text_or_blocker: The authors conclude that thrombin-activated PAR1 contributes to secondary injury and that APC acts through PAR1 by biased agonism to improve recovery after contusive SCI. This is a receptor-complex and functional-output record; it is not evidence of purified ligand-receptor affinity or a terminal TF pathway.
context_and_limitations: Direct SCI functional causality is strong for PAR1 genotype and APC treatment interaction. EPCR contribution, endogenous APC release, purified binding, and intracellular pathway identity remain unresolved; thrombin and APC branches must remain distinct.

observation_value_or_blocker: In adult rats with complete T9 spinal cord transection, Substance P immunoreactivity was increased in the L6-S1 sacral parasympathetic nucleus relative to intact rats. In conscious cystometry, intrathecal NK1 antagonist L-733060 at 30-100 micrograms blocked or reduced post-injury spinal micturition reflexes in most SCI rats, with little or no effect in intact controls.
